name: Vivienne Westwood
founded: Shop at 430 King's Road, 1971 (Let It Rock). SEX 1974. Seditionaries Dec 1976–1980. World's End from 1980/81.
founders: Vivienne Westwood (designer) + Malcolm McLaren (partner, later Sex Pistols manager). McLaren was the shop/idea partner; Westwood cut and made the clothes.
card_sub: King’s Road 1971 · SEX · Seditionaries · World’s End
story: Westwood and McLaren were bored of late-60s hippie London and obsessed with 1950s rebellion. In 1971 McLaren, dressed in a powder-blue teddy-boy suit, ducked into a King’s Road phone box in the rain; a shop owner across the street at 430 invited him in, then vanished and left him the keys. Westwood started knocking up Teddy Boy clothes, then biker leather, then rubber.

In 1974 they bolted huge pink padded letters spelling SEX onto the facade. December 1976 they reopened as Seditionaries: Clothes for Heroes — bondage straps, tartan, zips. After the Pistols collapsed they refitted the shop as World’s End and in 1981 showed Pirate, Westwood’s first official catwalk collection.
style_codes: Bondage trousers with hobble straps and towelling bum-flap
Parachute shirts, tartan, safety-pin and slogan tees

Attitude: confrontational, romantic-primitive, clothes as protest

quotes.text: It changed the way people looked. I was messianic about punk, seeing if one could put a spoke in the system in some way. I realised there was no subversion without ideas. It’s not enough to want to destroy everything.

If you invest in art, if you study yourself, you become a freedom fighter immediately because your life changes, you get off the consumer treadmill, and you start thinking. My thing as a fashion designer [is] I said buy less clothes. Keep wearing things that you’ve really chosen that you really love. That is status. It’s not that you have to keep consuming. A status symbol is a book.
